lean.statement: theorem exists_functorial_object_injective_resolution {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (J : C ⥤ C) (η : 𝟭 C ⟶ J) (hη : ∀ A : C, Mono (η.app A)) (hJ : ∀ A : C, Injective (J.obj A)) : ∃ (E : C ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ) (ε : (CochainComplex.single₀ C) ⟶ E), (∀ A : C, QuasiIso (ε.app A)) ∧ (∀ (A B : C), E.map (0 : A ⟶ B) = 0) ∧ IsZero (E.obj (0 : C)) ∧ (∀ (A : C) (n : ℕ), Injective ((E.obj A).X n))

title: Functorial objectwise injective resolutions
statement: For an abelian category C, a functorial monomorphic embedding η : 𝟭 C ⟶ J into injective objects admits a functor E : C ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ and a natural augmentation ε : single₀ C ⟶ E such that each ε.app A is a quasi-isomorphism, E maps every zero morphism to zero, E.obj 0 is a zero complex, and every term (E.obj A).X n is injective.

proof.text: Let K(A) be the kernel of J(A) → J(0). Kernel maps make K a functor, and naturality of η lifts it to a monomorphic natural transformation ι : id → K. Factor a zero map A → B through 0 to show that K sends it to zero. The splitting J(0) → J(A) of J(A) → J(0) gives a retraction onto K(A), explicitly by lifting id − ps to the kernel. Thus K(A) is injective by CategoryTheory.Retract.injective. All these constructions and identities are proved in the private normalized helpers.

Define the quotient functor Q(A) = coker(ι_A), using cokernel.map for its maps. It preserves zero morphisms because K does. Set Q₀ = id and Qₙ₊₁ = Qₙ ⋙ Q. Define E(A)ⁿ = K(Qₙ(A)), with differential the quotient projection followed by ι at Qₙ₊₁(A). The cokernel condition proves d² = 0; naturality of the projections and ι gives the complex maps and their identity and composition laws. The same naturality gives ε : single₀ → E with component ι in degree zero.

For a morphism f and a monomorphism g out of coker(f), exactness of (f, coker.π(f) ≫ g) follows from ShortComplex.exact_cokernel and ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono. Apply this at each ι. In positive degrees, precompose the first map by the preceding quotient epimorphism and use the same exactness comparison. In degree zero the augmentation is monomorphic and its image is the kernel of d⁰. CochainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_zeros prove the degree-zero assertion; positive-degree exactness and exactness of single₀ in positive degrees prove that each ε_A is a quasi-isomorphism.

Every Qₙ and K preserves zero morphisms, so E does degreewise. Applying E to id₀ = 0 proves that E(0) is zero. Each term is K applied to an object, hence injective by the retraction argument. Package E and ε with these four proved properties.
